concept.name: Deep in-the-money option
concept.definition: A deep in-the-money option is an option whose strike is far enough inside the money that its time value is negligible and its price moves almost one-for-one with the underlying (delta near +1 for calls, -1 for puts). 'Deep' is an informal descriptor with no fixed regulatory threshold.
concept.intuition: A deep ITM option behaves almost like a leveraged surrogate for the stock itself, with most of its value being intrinsic.
concept.mechanics: Premium approximates intrinsic value plus minimal time value; gamma, vega, and theta are near zero. Deep ITM American calls on dividend stocks and deep ITM puts are the prime early-exercise candidates because remaining time value can fall below the value of capturing the dividend or strike interest.
concept.failure_modes: Deep ITM strikes are often illiquid with wide bid-ask spreads, so entry/exit costs can exceed the residual time value. Deep ITM European options can trade below intrinsic value due to discounting.
concept.misconceptions: Deep ITM calls are not identical to owning stock: they receive no dividends, and holders must still act (sell or exercise) before expiration; brokers may also auto-exercise them, creating an unintended stock position.
concept.example: With stock at $150, the $100 call is deep ITM and might trade at $50.30 — $50 intrinsic value plus $0.30 time value, with delta near 1.0.

citations.source: CFTC Glossary — A Guide to the Language of the Futures Industry
